title.narrative: Promote Access to Finance, Entrepreneurship and Employment in Mali

description.narrative: The development objective of the Promote Access to Finance, Entrepreneurship, and Employment in Mali Project for Mali is to improve access to finance, entrepreneurship, and income generating activities for vulnerable segments in Mali. The project comprises of five components. The first component is promoting sustainable financial inclusion and fintech development. It consists of following sub-components: (i) strengthen the supervision and performance of the microfinance sector; (ii) increase usage of transaction accounts and support fintech uptake; and (iii) improving financial education and consumer protection. The second component is provision of risk-sharing and capacity-building for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It consists of following sub-components: (i) provide risk-sharing through the private guarantee fund; and (ii) providing tailored capacity-building to MSMEs for addressing existing structural gaps and Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) related challenges. The third component is support income-generating activities (IGA) and employment. It consists of following sub-components: (i) support IGAs; and (ii) labor-intensive public works program. The fourth component, contingent emergency response (CERC) aims to provide flexibility to re-focus the scope of the activities, in case of a natural disaster, security, emergency and or catastrophic events, which will be triggered following proclamation of a state of emergency or declaration of disaster. The fifth component, project management and implementation support provide resources to support project management and overall project implementation.
To improve access to finance, entrepreneurship and income generating activities for vulnerable segments in Mali.

The Recipient shall maintain, throughout the Project implementation period, a project implementation unit (“PIU”), within the MEF,with composition, mandate and resources satisfactory to the Association. To this end, the PIU shall: i) recruit no later than 3months after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain, a financial management specialist and an accountant, each withqualifications, experience and terms of reference shall be acceptable to the Association;

The Recipient shall, no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintain, throughout theProject implementation period, with composition, mandate and resources satisfactory to the Association, a technical committee, tobe responsible for guiding and monitoring the implementation of Part 2.1.3 of the Project, including, inter alia: (a) providingguidance to the PSGF SA, and (b) adopting guarantee policies and guidelines applicable to Part 2.1.3 of the Project; and as furtherdetailed in the Risk Sharing Facility Procedure Manual.

The Recipient shall, not later than two (2) months after the Effective Date, establish and thereafter maintain, throughout theProject implementation period, with composition, mandate and resources satisfactory to the Association, a steering committee, to bechaired by Minister of Economy and Finance or his/her representative, and to be comprised of, inter alia, representatives of theRecipient's ministries responsible for MSMEs, employment, digital economy respectively, and representatives of the central bank,the association of banks and financial institutions (ABFI) and the professional association of decentralized financial system(ADFS) (“Steering Committee”).
